title: 42-inch compact desk nook
monitorArmNote: Use a clamp mount only if the rear edge accepts it.
footrestNote: A compact footrest should leave room to slide both feet back.
tradeoff: A full-size keyboard and mouse take most of the working width. Move storage off the desktop.
clearanceNote: Check trim and outlet plugs before centering the top.

title: 48-inch small apartment setup
monitorArmNote: Use a clamp arm to free the rear portion of the shallow top.
footrestNote: Measure below the frame if a footrest needs to slide inward.
tradeoff: A 30-inch top leaves only 28 inches behind it in this room.
clearanceNote: Measure the space from the desktop front edge to the closest obstruction.

title: 60-inch dual-monitor workstation
monitorArmNote: This scenario assumes two displays on stands. Check combined stand width.
footrestNote: Keep the platform under the keyboard position in a centered layout.
tradeoff: The wider top holds two screens, but a side cabinet can consume the extra wall width.
clearanceNote: Tape out the chair zone and verify the screens fit with their stands turned.

title: Narrow-room chair clearance
monitorArmNote: An arm can reclaim desktop space, but it cannot create rear room clearance.
footrestNote: An oversized platform can block feet from sliding out while standing up.
tradeoff: This target leaves 31 inches behind the top, one inch below the planning allowance.
clearanceNote: Try a different wall or remove a rear obstruction before ordering.

title: Studio apartment corner desk
monitorArmNote: Check the mount swing against both walls before tightening the clamp.
footrestNote: Use a compact platform where the chair naturally centers.
tradeoff: A corner saves an open wall but can constrain cable access and chair rotation.
clearanceNote: Mark the rectangle from the widest wall trim and keep the door swing clear.

title: 48-inch dual-monitor desk
monitorArmNote: Two stands need enough width for inward screen angles.
footrestNote: Avoid placing the platform against a desk crossbar.
tradeoff: Two displays may fit with little room left for speakers or a laptop.
clearanceNote: Measure outside bezel width and stand depth, with the panels angled as used.

title: Shared bedroom desk
monitorArmNote: Check the wall gap before using a clamp and measure reach with the screen in place.
footrestNote: Confirm a footrest stays within the frame opening and away from the bed path.
tradeoff: Furniture across the room may block chair roll-back even when the walls measure wide enough.
clearanceNote: Use the distance to the bed frame as the rear boundary.

title: Alcove desk with side walls
monitorArmNote: Allow room to tighten a clamp and adjust the screen if both sides are enclosed.
footrestNote: Keep the foot support centered and test side-to-side leg movement.
tradeoff: A nearly wall-to-wall top limits installation access and cable routing.
clearanceNote: Measure width at desktop height and again at the floor for the feet.

title: Ultrawide home office
monitorArmNote: Check monitor weight, VESA pattern and depth against mount limits.
footrestNote: Test clearance with the desk at its lowest preset if adding foot support.
tradeoff: A curved panel can project forward, cutting into viewing distance.
clearanceNote: Set the screen position with the desktop mocked up before drilling or clamping.

title: Under-window workstation
monitorArmNote: Position the arm so no hardware touches the sash or blinds.
footrestNote: Test whether a footrest sits flat away from heaters or floor vents.
tradeoff: A window can limit maximum lift or increase screen glare.
clearanceNote: Open the window and raise the monitor and desk through their full travel.

title: Wall desk for a petite user
monitorArmNote: A compact display on a compatible mount leaves keyboard space.
footrestNote: Measure the lift needed under the fixed top before choosing a platform.
tradeoff: A small top can fit the room while its fixed height misses the seated elbow target.
clearanceNote: Verify seat depth and keyboard height as separate requirements.

title: Tall-user apartment workstation
monitorArmNote: Ensure the display reaches eye height at both desk presets.
footrestNote: Leave room for long legs before adding any under-desk accessory.
tradeoff: Cable trays and crossbars can reduce knee space even when the desk rises high enough.
clearanceNote: Check both the desk’s full height travel and its clear space below the top.

title: Living-room work-from-home desk
monitorArmNote: A clamp can free space, but confirm the desk edge can support it.
footrestNote: Keep the platform fully under the top when the chair is tucked.
tradeoff: The desk can fit with a narrow margin, while seating or a walkway may encroach.
clearanceNote: Test the layout with someone walking behind the chair.

title: Spare-room large standing desk
monitorArmNote: Dual stands are assumed. Measure actual monitor separation and cable reach.
footrestNote: Try foot placement with the desk legs at their final span.
tradeoff: Wide tops simplify screen placement but may block a closet or door at the edge.
clearanceNote: Measure the clear wall with doors fully open and mark chair travel.

title: Hallway office nook
monitorArmNote: A shallow arm layout improves desktop use only if swing stays out of the walkway.
footrestNote: Keep any platform out of the circulation path.
tradeoff: Only 24 inches remain behind the target desk. The chair zone overlaps the path.
clearanceNote: Check a different wall or use this area for standing tasks without a parked chair.
